skill.name: relight
skill.description: Relight still images with the RunComfy CLI. Use Qwen Edit 2509 Relight LoRA or related edit models to change lighting direction, color temperature, intensity, and mood while preserving the subject.
skill.summary: Change image lighting with RunComfy while preserving the subject.
skill.author: runcomfy-com

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown backticks, code fences, and visible documentation links rather than executable code. No prompt injection attempt or covert exfiltration was found. The remaining concerns are unpinned CLI installation guidance and disclosed external processing of user images and prompts.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the @runcomfy/cli version or require explicit user confirmation before installation or npx execution.
Ask for user confirmation before uploading images or prompts, and link to RunComfy data handling and retention terms.
Document logout and token removal steps, keep mode 0600, and prefer scoped environment tokens in CI.
Keep Bash permissions limited to runcomfy commands and avoid adding general shell or package-manager permissions.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned CLI Installation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill suggests installing or running @runcomfy/cli from the package registry without a pinned version. This creates a supply-chain and host mutation risk if followed by an agent or user.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The install commands and package-manager guidance are explicit. The risk is moderate because the package is named and the skill warns against arbitrary remote install scripts.

semantic_findings.title: External Processing of User Images and Prompts
semantic_findings.description: The documented workflow posts user images and prompts to RunComfy model APIs, polls status, and downloads generated results. This is intended behavior but has privacy impact for sensitive source images.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly states that the CLI posts to the Model API and lists outbound RunComfy endpoints. No covert exfiltration is evident, but external processing is clear.

content.value_statement: Image teams often need new lighting without reshooting a photo. This skill routes relighting prompts through RunComfy models for controlled lighting changes.
actual_capabilities: Routes dedicated relighting jobs to Qwen Edit 2509 Relight LoRA.
Uses RunComfy CLI commands for model execution and result download.
Supports prompt guidance for lighting direction, temperature, softness, and contrast.
Suggests fallback edit models for broader image edits with lighting changes.
Provides examples for products, portraits, landscapes, references, and batch galleries.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a valid RunComfy login or token.
Processes still images only; it does not relight video through this skill.
Uploads user images and prompts to RunComfy model endpoints.
Results depend on model behavior and may need iterative prompt refinement.

use_cases.title: Catalog Product Relighting
use_cases.description: Create warmer or softer product lighting without arranging a new studio setup.

use_cases.title: Portrait Mood Changes
use_cases.description: Shift portrait lighting from neutral, overcast, or flat light into a stronger mood.

use_cases.title: Creative Direction Tests
use_cases.description: Compare different lighting concepts before committing to a shoot or final edit.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Product Relight
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one product image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Relight this product image with soft window light from the left. Preserve product shape, color, framing, and background.

prompt_templates.title: Portrait Golden Hour
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for portrait mood adjustment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Change this portrait to warm golden hour lighting. Add a soft key light from front-left and preserve identity and pose.

prompt_templates.title: Reference Lighting Match
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using a lighting reference image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the lighting direction, color temperature, and contrast from the reference image. Preserve the original subject and composition.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Gallery Consistency
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a product gallery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Relight every image in this SKU gallery with consistent warm studio lighting, soft shadows, and preserved product color.

output_examples.input: A product photo has flat white-box lighting and weak shadows.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Qwen Edit Relight with warm window light, soft side shadows, and explicit product preservation.

output_examples.input: A portrait should look like late afternoon sunlight while keeping the same face and pose.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests a golden-hour prompt with warm key light, gentle rim light, and identity preservation language.

output_examples.input: A scene needs a lighting change plus a background adjustment.
output_examples.output: The skill routes the task to a broader image edit model instead of the dedicated relight endpoint.

best_practices: State lighting direction, color temperature, intensity, and preservation requirements clearly.
Use user-approved image URLs and confirm that external processing is acceptable.
Start with one image before applying the same lighting prompt to a batch.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague prompts such as make it better without lighting details.
Do not upload private images unless the user has approved external processing.
Do not use this still-image skill for video relighting workflows.

faq.question: What does this skill relight?
faq.answer: It relights still images by changing lighting direction, color temperature, intensity, contrast, and mood.

faq.question: Which model does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers Qwen Edit 2509 Relight LoRA for dedicated lighting changes.

faq.question: Can it preserve the subject?
faq.answer: Yes, prompts should explicitly ask to preserve identity, pose, framing, and color when that matters.

faq.question: Does it need a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes, the RunComfy CLI must be installed and authenticated before model runs can complete.

faq.question: Will images leave my machine?
faq.answer: Yes, the RunComfy CLI sends images and prompts to RunComfy model endpoints for processing.

faq.question: Can it relight videos?
faq.answer: No, this skill describes still-image relighting. Video workflows require separate RunComfy workflows.
